engineering.title: Engineering dashboard
engineering.meta.description: Real numbers on how I build this site: the tests of every build, specs with their commits, deployments, evals and AI spend.
engineering.lead: Everything comes from the repo and the build: nothing is typed by hand. When a number is missing, I say so instead of showing one.
engineering.timezone: Dates and times are Colombia time (America/Bogota).
engineering.deploy.title: This deployment
engineering.deploy.passed: {passed} of {total} unit and contract tests passed in this build, across {files} files.
engineering.deploy.passedShort: {passed} of {total} unit and contract tests passed in this build.
engineering.deploy.noReport: No test report in this build.
engineering.deploy.ranAt: Vitest ran on {date}, before the build.
engineering.deploy.source: Vercel's system variables (VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA and VERCEL_ENV) and the Vitest JSON report the prebuild leaves in .engineering/vitest.json, read when this page was built.
engineering.specs.title: From spec to commit
engineering.specs.intro: Each spec with its status, its requirements, the commits that name it and the days to its first feat. Open one to see its commits and which requirements a test names.
engineering.specs.history: History as of {date}, commit {sha}, with {count} non-merge commits.
engineering.specs.noHistory: No versioned history: there are no commits or dates to show.
engineering.specs.rule: A commit counts for a spec when its subject names it in parentheses, like feat(030): …; when it names several, like fix(018, 022): …, it counts for each. A requirement belongs to a spec when its number starts with the spec's: FR-4501 belongs to 045.
engineering.specs.titlesNote: Titles and subjects come straight from the repo, in Spanish.
engineering.specs.source: the «Estado:» line of each spec.md, the versioned .md files of each folder and content/engineering/history.json, which I take locally with git on every wave push.
engineering.detail.metaDescription: The commits of spec {number}, its requirements named by a test and the days to its first feat, taken from the repo.
engineering.detail.timeline: From the spec to its first feat
engineering.detail.daysRule: I count calendar days in Colombia, from the commit that added the spec main file to the first feat commit that names it.
engineering.detail.noStatusLine: This folder has no «Estado:» line in a spec.md.
engineering.detail.notCreated: No creation date in the history
engineering.detail.days.one: {count} day from the spec to its first feat.
engineering.detail.days.other: {count} days from the spec to its first feat.
engineering.detail.noDays: No days to built: one of the two dates is missing, or the first feat predates the spec.
engineering.detail.requirements: Requirements named by a test: {tested} of {total}
engineering.detail.noRequirements: This folder declares no FR- or SC- requirements.
engineering.tests.title: Tests that run on every build
engineering.tests.runs: The Vercel build runs the Vitest ones before compiling; the e2e ones run with Playwright locally.
engineering.tests.trace: {tested} of {total} spec requirements (FR- and SC-) are named by at least one test.
engineering.tests.notCoverage: This is traceability, not coverage: I look for each id written literally in tests/, not for executed lines.
engineering.tests.source: the versioned files of specs/ and tests/ ({method}), counted on {date}, when this page was built.
engineering.tests.method.tree: the build tree, a clean clone of the repo
engineering.delivery.title: Delivery: commits and deployments
engineering.delivery.chartTitle: {total} commits in {weeks} weeks; the busiest week had {max}.
engineering.delivery.noWeekly: No versioned history: there are no weekly commits to show.
engineering.delivery.weeklySource: content/engineering/history.json, with non-merge commits up to {date}, per Monday-to-Sunday week.
engineering.delivery.noDeploys: No deployment data: the history was taken without the GitHub CLI.
engineering.delivery.deploysSource: GitHub's deployments API, queried on {date} with the GitHub CLI, without preview URLs.
engineering.evals.title: Evals that measure the agents
engineering.evals.how: I run it with {command} ({cost}); it never runs on its own in the build.
engineering.evals.invalid: The results file doesn't match the 032 schema ({reason}), so I show no numbers.
engineering.evals.source: {file}, validated against the 032 EvalResults schema at build time.
engineering.spend.title: AI spend against the cap
engineering.spend.intro: The monthly target is {target} USD and the hard cap is {cap} USD, adding up every AI provider.
engineering.spend.live: These numbers are read from the rate-limit counters, cached for up to an hour. They store nothing about visitors.
engineering.spend.noscript: Without JavaScript this section doesn't load: the same numbers are in the JSON.
engineering.spend.unavailable: Not available right now: I couldn't read the counters.
engineering.spend.today: Estimate for the last 24 hours: {usd} USD ({cop} COP)
engineering.spend.todayNote: It's an estimate from Gemini uses: each use at its typical cost. The real monthly spend, per provider, arrives with 043.
engineering.spend.overTarget: It's already over the monthly target.
engineering.spend.mcp: Calls to the public MCP in the last 24 hours: {count}
engineering.spend.mcpNote: If the 044 MCP isn't published yet, this counter is zero.
engineering.spend.takenAt: Counted on {date}; pesos at the {rateDate} TRM rate ({rate} COP per dollar).
engineering.budgets.title: Budgets a test watches
engineering.budgets.intro: The ones in principle V of the constitution, measured on a mid-range mobile profile.
engineering.budgets.a11yNote: The accessibility test watches for zero critical or serious violations with axe; no test in the repo computes the 95 score.
engineering.budgets.source: the budgets in .specify/memory/constitution.md and, when they exist, the measurements I saved in content/engineering/history.json from runs I was doing anyway.
